subject: math
title: Compare Three-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 2 Comparing Three-Digit Numbers Worksheets: Greater Than, Less Than and Ordering to 1000
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standard_text: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 comparing numbers worksheets: compare three-digit numbers with base-ten blocks and place-value charts, use the greater than, less than and equal symbols, put numbers in order, and solve word problems. 100 practice questions with explanations.
key_big: Look at the hundreds first. If they are the same, compare the tens, then the ones.
key_sub: 301 > 299, because 3 hundreds is more than 2 hundreds. The open side of > and < faces the greater number: 452 > 425 and 425 < 452.
body_html:
Hundreds are worth the most

A three-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones. One hundred is the same as 10 tens. So the hundreds count the most. Always look at the hundreds first.

Compare hundreds, then tens, then ones

  1. Look at the hundreds. More hundreds means a greater number.
  2. Same hundreds? Look at the tens.
  3. Same tens too? Look at the ones.
Example

Compare 405 and 450.

Both have 4 hundreds. Tens: 405 has 0 tens and 450 has 5 tens. 0 is less than 5.

Answer: 405 is less than 450

The symbols >, < and =

SymbolSayExample
>is greater than452 > 425
<is less than405 < 450
=is equal to500 + 7 = 507

Tip: the open side of > and < always faces the greater number. The point faces the smaller number.

Put numbers in order

Compare two numbers at a time. Find the least one first, then the next, then the greatest.

Example

Put 352, 235 and 325 in order from least to greatest.

235 has only 2 hundreds, so it is the least. 325 and 352 both have 3 hundreds. Tens: 2 < 5, so 325 < 352.

Answer: 235, 325, 352

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Comparing the ones first: “362 < 326, because 2 < 6”Start with the hundreds, then the tens: 362 > 326
Thinking big digits win: “199 > 301”Hundreds first: 1 hundred < 3 hundreds, so 199 < 301
Skipping a zero: “405 is the same as 450”405 has 0 tens; 450 has 5 tens. 405 < 450
Turning the symbol the wrong way: 452 < 425The open side faces the greater number: 452 > 425
Ordering backwardsLeast to greatest starts with the smallest number

faq.q: How do you compare three-digit numbers in 2nd grade?
faq.a: Look at the hundreds first; the number with more hundreds is greater. If the hundreds are the same, compare the tens, and if those are the same too, compare the ones.

faq.q: What is an easy way to remember greater than and less than?
faq.a: The open side of the symbol always faces the greater number, and the point faces the smaller one. So 452 > 425 and 425 < 452.

faq.q: Why do kids think 199 is greater than 301?
faq.a: They see the big 9s and forget that the hundreds digit counts the most. 199 has only 1 hundred and 301 has 3 hundreds, so 199 < 301.

faq.q: How do you compare numbers with a zero, like 405 and 450?
faq.a: A zero means none in that place. Both have 4 hundreds, but 405 has 0 tens and 450 has 5 tens, so 405 < 450.
